item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 9, 2026
item.description:
With the latest from across the media business, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Media Jobs Report welcomes Studiio as one of its newest Pro Members. Based in Melbourne, Australia, Studiio provides listener engagement and station management technology used by more than 100 radio stations worldwide. The platform handles more than one million SMS messages each month and offers tools for messaging, scheduling, audience engagement, and station operations. Learn more about Studiio and the companies supporting the media industry at Media Jobs Report dot com.
In audience ratings news,
Nielsen reports 31.2 million Americans watched primetime coverage of the 2026 midterm elections, up nearly 23 percent from 2022. Broadcast networks attracted 57 percent of viewers, while cable networks captured 43 percent. Viewership peaked at 32.4 million during the 9:30 Eastern half-hour. Adults 55 and older accounted for nearly two-thirds of the audience.
Turning to radio,
Canada's broadcast regulator has launched a free music database to help radio stations identify Canadian songs and meet content requirements. The CRTC says the downloadable resource combines information from multiple industry sources and will expand to include more French, Indigenous and third-language music. The database is designed to simplify programming and help Canadian artists gain exposure.
On the business side of media,
Fox Corporation has completed its acquisition of Roku, combining the streaming platform with Tubi and FOX One. Roku will continue operating as an open platform for viewers and content partners. Fox expects the deal to generate about 400 million dollars in annual cost savings within two years.
Turning to the next generation of media professionals,
The University of Missouri School of Journalism has named master's student Laiba Khan Zai the 35th David Kaplan Memorial Fellow. Zai will receive a $10,000 stipend and spend the spring semester working full-time at ABC News' Washington Bureau. The fellowship honors ABC News Producer David Kaplan, who was killed while covering the war in Bosnia in 1992.
In media education news,
The FCC has extended its filing deadline for new noncommercial educational FM translator applications to November 23 at 6 p.m. Eastern. The extension follows technical problems with the agency's Licensing Management System. The FCC says the new deadline will be strictly enforced, and the related filing freeze will remain in place until the window closes.
In awards and recognition news,
Great Days Out on the Bus From Buxton took top honors at the 2026 Independent Podcast Awards, winning Podcast of the Year, Best Travel and Adventure, and Best Artwork. War Hall was named runner-up and won Best Arts and Culture and Best Music. More than 400 people attended the London ceremony. For the complete list of winners, log on to Media Jobs Report dot com.
In television news,
TelevisaUnivision and the Latin Recording Academy have announced more than 18 sponsors for the 2026 Latin GRAMMY Awards. First-time partners include Gilead Sciences, Rémy Martin, Ross and Valentino Beauty. The show airs November 12 on Univision and streams on ViX. Get more media news in the MJR Morning Brief.
And finally,
Phil Wickham leads the 2026 K-LOVE Fan Awards nominees with four nominations. Lauren Daigle, Jamie MacDonald, Jeremy Camp, Josiah Queen and Elevation Worship each earned three. Daigle and Sadie Robertson Huff hosted the May 24 ceremony in Nashville, which aired on TBN May 29. Robert Anthony Cruz of the Savannah Bananas was also honored with the Sports Impact Award.
For more industry news, the latest media jobs and free tools, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
